# Autoantibodies in rheumatic diseases

*Categories: Clinical knowledge > Internal medicine > Rheumatology and immunology > Basics of rheumatology > Autoantibodies in rheumatic diseases*

[Original Article Link](/library/ul0pAT)

---

## Summary

<u>Antibody</u> diagnostics play a vital role in the differential diagnosis of rheumatic diseases. Many of these <u>autoantibodies</u> can be differentiated into <u>antibodies</u> against nuclear <u>antigens</u> (<u>ANAs</u>) and <u>antibodies</u> against <u>cytoplasmic</u> <u>antigens</u> (<u>ANCAs</u>). Although both of these <u>antibodies</u> are detectable in numerous autoimmune diseases, elevated <u>ANAs</u> are typical for <u>connective tissue diseases</u> and elevated <u>ANCAs</u> for <u>vasculitis</u>. Diagnosis of individual conditions can be further supported by detecting disease-specific <u>ANAs</u> or <u>ANCAs</u>, such as <u>anti-dsDNA</u> in <u>systemic lupus erythematosus</u> or <u>c-ANCA</u> in <u>granulomatosis with polyangiitis</u>.

---

## Antinuclear antibodies (ANAs)

* Brief description

* <u>ANAs</u> comprise numerous <u>antibodies</u> against specific nuclear <u>antigens</u>.

* In addition, <u>ANAs</u> include <u>autoantibodies</u> against <u>DNA</u> and <u>histones</u>.

* Assessment

* Elevated <u>ANA</u> levels are observed in various autoimmune diseases, especially in the diseases listed below.

* An increase is typically observed in <u>connective tissue diseases</u>, but may also be found in, e.g., <u>rheumatoid arthritis</u> (<u>RA</u>), <u>autoimmune hepatitis</u>, and <u>vasculitides</u>.

* In general, elevated <u>ANA</u> levels are considered nonspecific; exact diagnosis requires determination of individual <u>antibodies</u>.





| Overview of ANAs |  |  |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <u>Connective tissue diseases</u> | Antigen-specific ANAs | Other <u>autoantibodies</u> |
| <br><u>Systemic lupus erythematosus</u> (<u>SLE</u>) | <br><br>* <u>Anti-dsDNA</u> (in ∼ 70% of cases)<br><br>* <u>Anti-Sm</u> (Smith)<br><br>* Anti-<u>histone</u> (in <u>drug-induced lupus erythematosus</u>)<br><br>* <u>Anti-Ro/SSA</u><br><br>* <u>Anti-La/SSB</u><br><br>* <u>Anti-U1 RNP</u> (ribonucleoprotein)<br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Antiphospholipid antibodies</u> (anti-<u>cardiolipin</u> most common type)<br><br>* Anti-C1q antibodies (correlates with disease activity)<br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Systemic sclerosis</u> (<u>scleroderma</u>) | <br>* <u>Anti-Scl-70</u> (anti-<u>topoisomerase</u> <u>antibody</u> I: seen in 30–70% of cases<br><br> | <br><br>* Anticentromere<br><br>* <u>Anti-RNA polymerase III</u><br><br><br> |
| Sjögren syndrome | <br><br>* <u>Anti-Ro/SSA</u><br><br>* <u>Anti-La/SSB</u><br><br>* 60–80% of patients positive for one or both <u>antibodies</u><br><br><br> | <br><br>* <u>Rheumatoid factor</u> (RF); present in > 50% of patients<br><br>* <u>Anti-CCP</u><br><br>* <u>Salivary gland</u> <u>antibodies</u><br><br><br> |
| <br><u>Polymyositis</u> and <u>dermatomyositis</u><br> | <br><br>* <u>Anti-Jo1</u><br><br>* <u>Anti-Mi2</u><br><br><br> | <br>* RF<br><br> |
| <u>Mixed connective tissue disease</u> | <br>* Anti-U1-RNP<br><br> | <br>* RF<br><br> |





References:[[1]](/library/RQalD4)[[2]](/library/Z5aZiO)

## Antineutrophil cytoplasmic antibodies (ANCAs)

* Description: <u>ANCAs</u> comprise <u>antibodies</u> against specific <u>cytoplasmic</u> <u>antigens</u>

* Assessment

* An increase is observed in various autoimmune diseases, especially <u>vasculitides</u>

* Atypical fluorescence patterns of <u>p-ANCA</u> (<u>perinuclear ANCA</u>) also play an important role in the diagnosis of <u>primary sclerosing cholangitis</u> (<u>PSC</u>).





| Specific <u>ANCA</u> | Diseases |
| --- | --- |
| <br>c-ANCA<br>(Proteinase-3<u>antibody</u>) | <br><br>* <u>Granulomatosis with polyangiitis</u>: ∼ 90% of patients are <u>ANCA</u> positive (mostly <u>c-ANCA</u>).<br><br>* Rarely in <u>microscopic polyangiitis</u>, <u>Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis</u>, <u>infective endocarditis</u> [[3]](/library/N9X-nZ0)<br><br><br> |
| <br>p-ANCA<br>(<u>Myeloperoxidase</u> <u>antibody</u>) | <br><br>* <u>Microscopic polyangiitis</u>: ∼ 70% of patients are <u>ANCA</u> positive (mostly <u>p-ANCA</u>).<br><br>* <u>Eosinophilic granulomatosis with polyangiitis</u>: ∼ 50% of patients are <u>ANCA</u> positive (both <u>c-ANCA</u> and <u>p-ANCA</u>).<br><br>* Rarely: <u>polyarteritis nodosa</u>, <u>granulomatosis with polyangiitis</u><br><br><br> |
| atypical <u>p-ANCA</u> | <br><br>* <u>PSC</u><br><br>* <u>Ulcerative colitis</u><br><br>* Rarely: <u>primary biliary cholangitis</u>, <u>Crohn's disease</u><br><br><br> |
